questions.q: Let $a, b$ and $c$ be any real numbers. Suppose that there are real numbers $x, y$ and $z$ not all zero such that $x = c y + b z \text{,} y = a z + c x$ and $z = b x + a y$, then $a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + 2 a b c$ is equal to
questions.solution:
System of equations

$\begin{cases}x - c y - b z = 0 & & & \\ c x - y + a z = 0 & \\ b x + a y - z = 0 & & \end{cases}$

has non trivial solution if the determinant of coefficient matrix is zero.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & - c & - b \\ c & - 1 & a \\ b & a & - 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1 \left(1 - a^{2}\right) + c \left(- c - a b\right) - b \left(c a + b\right) = 0$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + 2 a b c = 1$

Expanding the above with respect to~${R}_{1}$,~we get,

If \(\lambda ≠ 8\) and \(\mu \in R\), then system of linear equations has unique solution. And, if \(\lambda=8\) and \(\mu=15\), then system of linear equations has infinite number of solutions, because \(\Delta_2=3 \lambda-2 \mu+6\) is also be zero. Hence, option (2) is correct.
